findings.title: The danger colour is used on a page whose spec says it appears nowhere on it
findings.evidence: rose is used three times: the 'The app you tried' label (landing-comparisons.tsx:140), the N75,000.00 figure in that card (:194), and the dot marking a debt you owe (landing-three-things.tsx:77). The addendum reserves rose for money going wrong, and docs/06-page-specs.md:492 states 'The danger colour appears nowhere on this page.' The 1440 and 390 boards draw all three in red, so the design and the written rule disagree and the build followed the design without the disagreement being recorded.
findings.fix: Name the conflict in docs/open-items.md for the designer and the spec owner: either the boards' red becomes a non-danger tone, or the addendum's reservation gains an exception for a marketing surface where no figure is anyone's money and the spec sentence goes. Do not change the colour until one of them is decided.

findings.title: At 1440 the Mizaniya side of each comparison can only be revealed with a pointer
findings.evidence: The reveal is '.reveal-host:hover .reveal-over, .reveal-host:focus-within .reveal-over'. Nothing inside a comparison column is focusable - the claim is an h3 and both cards are plain divs - so :focus-within can never match, and a sighted keyboard-only reader at 1440 never sees half of each comparison. The content is in the DOM and is read by a screen reader, so this is a sighted-keyboard gap rather than a screen-reader one.
findings.fix: Give each column one focus stop that reveals (a focusable summary, or the column itself with an accessible name), or drop the hover gate at 1440 as the phone does and show both.

findings.title: Money is formatted by hand in seven places on one page
findings.evidence: The kobo treatment - a figure followed by a smaller, lighter span holding '.00' - is written out separately in safe-to-spend-card.tsx:17, landing-deck.tsx:54, landing-comparisons.tsx:194, landing-three-things.tsx:87 and :106, and rest-cards.tsx:41, :124 and :138, each with its own size and opacity. ui/ngn.tsx and ui/money-text.tsx already own this treatment elsewhere in the app, and the landing page uses neither. A change to how kobo is set has eight places to find.
findings.fix: Extend Ngn, or add one landing money component beside it, that takes the naira part and the kobo and owns the size, weight and opacity; use it everywhere on the page.

findings.title: Two progress bars restate a seed amount as a hand-written decimal
findings.evidence: Rail value={0.53} stands for 475,000 of 900,000, which is 0.5278, and rest-cards.tsx:48 Rail value={0.25} stands for 30,000 repaid of 120,000. Neither decimal names the amounts it comes from, and the first is rounded, so the bar and the figure beside it can drift apart without anything failing.
findings.fix: Name the two fractions in landing-copy.ts beside the figures they come from, with the division written in the comment, so the bar and the figure move together.

findings.title: Three landing component files are over the 150-line limit
findings.evidence: landing-comparisons.tsx is 233 lines, rest-cards.tsx 153 and landing-three-things.tsx 151, against REACT-03's 150. The rule is deferred on this project (standards_for_file: enforced false, 'REACT-03 is deferred, so it only reports for now'), with ITEM-2 attached to clear the backlog of them.
findings.fix: Split along the design's own structure rather than at a line count, as ITEM-2 records: the three comparison columns are three different bodies, and rest-cards.tsx holds four independent replicas.

findings.title: The carousel collapses two independent pauses into one flag
findings.evidence: resting is set true by a hidden tab (use-carousel.ts:72) and by a pointer or focus entering the rail (:82-85), and set false by either leaving. Returning to a tab while the pointer is still over the rail sets resting false and the rail advances under the pointer, which is the state the pointer pause exists to prevent.
findings.fix: Keep the two reasons apart - two booleans, or a set of reasons to pause - and rest while either holds.

findings.title: The rail's step assumes a gap that is written in another file
findings.evidence: The step is the card's measured width plus a literal 16 for the gap, and the comment above it says the width is measured 'so a change to the card width in the design cannot silently desynchronise the step' - which is true of the width and not of the gap. The gap is gap-16 in how-it-works-rail.tsx:86 and :88. A design change to the gap desynchronises the rail silently, which is exactly what the comment claims is prevented.
findings.fix: Read the gap from the scroller's computed style, or pass it in from the component that sets the class, and correct the comment.

findings.title: The hero screenshot chooses its theme from the system, not from the app's own theme
findings.evidence: The picture element switches on media='(prefers-color-scheme: dark)', while every other value on the page follows the app's theme, which is data-theme on the root (app/use-theme.ts, applied over tokens.css:95 and :124). Somebody who chose light on a device whose system is dark gets a light page carrying the dark screenshot, and the reverse.
findings.fix: Render one img and swap its source with a CSS rule keyed to the same two selectors the tokens use, or render both and hide one by those selectors, so the screenshot follows the page.

findings.title: The six faults the browser comparison found ship without a check
findings.evidence: This branch fixed a money face set in JetBrains Mono, a board label printed inside the hero image, a caption drawn across the pile, a clipped replica and a missing word of board copy. None of them has a test, and the comparison that found them was run by hand from a scratch script, so the same class of fault returns silently.
findings.fix: The acceptance journey the addendum plans in Playwright (K1) is where a rendered check belongs. Two are assertable now without it: the face on the figure, and the words of the board's copy.

findings.title: Three functions in the change are past the length that should prompt a question
findings.evidence: LandingComparisons is 90 lines, HowItWorksRail 83 and useCarousel 66, against the project's TS-07 threshold of 60. TS-07 is deferred here (standards_for_file: enforced false, 'TS-07 is deferred, so it only reports for now'), so nothing fails the build. Two of the three are long for the same reason as F5: three comparison columns with three different bodies in one function.
findings.fix: Take the three columns out of LandingComparisons as named components, as ITEM-2 plans for the screens; useCarousel is four small effects and reads as its length rather than hiding anything.

summary: Pass, with 1 high, 2 medium and 7 low findings open. The high: at 1440 the Mizaniya side of each comparison is revealed only by a pointer, so a sighted keyboard reader never sees half of it (DES-10). The mediums: the danger colour is used where the spec says it is nowhere, the boards having drawn it; and money is formatted by hand in seven places while ui/ngn.tsx owns that treatment. Nothing was left unchecked.
